3 The Pandora’s Box Problem

Pandora-NI (non-obligatory inspection).

When inspection is non-obligatory, Pandora may select any unopened box, committing to it without paying the inspection cost, but accepting the risk that its realized value may disappoint (Doval, 2018). The optimal adaptive policy for this variant is NP-hard (Fu et al., 2023), so we use a tractable restriction to committing policies (Beyhaghi and Kleinberg, 2019). A committing policy designates a single box as “held out”: this box will not be opened, but may be selected as the final choice. The remaining boxes are searched via Pandora-OI, with the held-out box providing the initial outside option.22 2 The value of the best committing policy that holds out multiple boxes cannot exceed that of the best single-box policy (Beyhaghi and Kleinberg, 2019), so it suffices to evaluate all single-holdout policies, in addition to the obligatory inspection policy (no holdouts). These M + 1 policies are compared by simulating their performance via MC sampling.

4 Pandora’s Router

Experimental setup.

We evaluate Pandora’s Router on the three domains described in §2.1, and compare with the following methods:

  • •

    -only: Route using the cheap estimator only (never opening any box).

  • •

    -always: Route using the expensive estimator only (always opening all boxes).

  • •

    Top-: Always queries for the two models with highest (open the two expected best boxes).

  • •

    Coin flip: Query with probability ; route to the maximum observed (randomly open boxes).
